niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces with strong clarity and structure: readable hierarchy, clearly grouped sections, visible labels, and layouts that feel organized rather than fragmented. Often favors spacious spacing, rounded cards or controls, and card-based or modular presentation over flat lists or monolithic panels. Color preference is mixed by context, but the strongest recurring pattern is not simply light or dark; it is choosing the theme that creates better focus, contrast, and visual polish. The user repeatedly likes clear affordances, complete visible content, and richer information when it is well-structured. They also show a recurring preference for softer, more refined styling such as rounded corners, subtle depth, integrated overlays, and cohesive accent usage.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong hierarchy with prominent titles or hero values, supportive subtitles or labels, distinct sections, grouped content, and layouts where the reading order is obvious.
Prefers more open whitespace, generous padding, clearer separation between sections, and lower perceived crowding over dense or tightly stacked layouts.
Prefers information presented in cards, modular blocks, or separated rows with soft containment rather than flat lists, monolithic panels, or overlapping compositions.
Prefers softer rounded corners and pill-like controls over sharper, boxier, or more technical-looking shapes.
Prefers interfaces where text and supporting content are easy to read, with stronger contrast, clearer visibility, and less faint or low-contrast presentation.

Prefers visible, explicit, and content-rich UI treatment such as descriptive options, detailed plan features, fully shown forms, readable status cards, and concrete supporting detail rather than sparse or underspecified presentation.

Prefers a visually polished theme with cohesive accents, subtle depth or dimming, and a controlled mood that improves focus; this can be light or dark depending on which version feels more refined and isolating.
